highlights.title: GTA: San Andreas’ Bigfoot myth is a classic urban legend
highlights.summary: There is a Bigfoot in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas — at least, that's what I and many others believed. Some time after the game had been released, the rumour about the new Rockstar game featuring the legendary creature spread across the internet.
body: It's been 22 years since the game was released, and now we know that was only an urban legend. There's no Bigfoot in San Andreas (unfortunately). But we couldn't figure out that by ourselves when the rumor started. The year was 2004, and information about games was scarce compared to nowadays. There was no way for us to confirm the authenticity of the allegedly real photo of Bigfoot posted by user "xDaRkAnGel_2000x" on a gaming forum.

The lack of reliable sources made these theories seem even more plausible. Aside from a few print publications, you basically had to spend hours browsing forums and GameFAQs posts to read about games and learn more about them. If you grew up in countries outside major game development hubs like the U.S. or Europe, you had even fewer options. I remember using an old social network called Orkut, which was huge in Brazil, to ask for help in a Final Fantasy 10 group.
points: There is a Bigfoot in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas — at least, that's what I and many others believed.
It's been 22 years since the game was released, and now we know that was only an urban legend.
The year was 2004, and information about games was scarce compared to nowadays.

highlights.summary: Supercell is bringing Clash Royale to the tabletop with Clash Royale: The Grand Arena, a board game developed with Maestro Media, set to launch on Kickstarter on October 20, 2026.
body: Designed by David Gordon, Ryan Rodriguez, and TAM, the game supports two to four players who can deploy cards, attack opponents and send their towers across two lanes.
Players will compete to destroy towers and collect crowns, the player holding the most crowns in the end wins.

The tabletop adaptation aims to retain several mechanics from the mobile game, including card-based strategy. Players build eight-card decks around a chosen champion, whose evolution card remains with them throughout the game. Players can upgrade or add characters to their decks between battles.

“Clash Royale has earned its place as a leading mobile strategy game by challenging players to think tactically, adapt, and outsmart their opponents,” said Andrea Fasulo, head of licensing at Supercell. “With The Grand Arena, our ambition is to honour that competitive spirit and strategic depth, giving fans a fresh challenge worthy of the game they love.”

highlights.title: Meta removes language that may have allowed it to scrape news sites
highlights.summary: After backlash, Meta is updating its terms again to remove language that suggested it could scrape content from sites, including news sites, to train its AI. Specifically, the following language no longer appears on the commercial terms page: … Meta may use any content from such domains, web pages…
body: Language that experts say allowed the scraping of news sites to train its AI has been removed from Meta’s terms.

Many, including Neiman Lab and James Grimmelmann, a professor of digital and information law at Cornell, interpreted it as an attempt to give Meta the right to use content scraped from sites to train its AI products for free and supersede blocking instructions in a site’s robots.txt file.

“We’ve heard you and want to clarify: the crawling terms we consolidated only applied to our ads and business products, and we’ve clarified that in the terms themselves. It does not change how Meta uses web crawlers. As always, content owners can use robots.txt to signal their preferences. This is not about scraping news sites, and these updates don’t give us new rights that supersede those preferences.”

body: The production team has revealed that The Mad King will return to the stage in London in 2027.

Game of Thrones creator George R.R. Martin made the announcement on his blog in September. "I had a splendid time in Stratford-upon-Avon for the premiere of Duncan Macmillan and Dominic Cooke’s epic new stage production of Game of Thrones: The Mad King," Martin wrote, "and furthermore, I’m thrilled to announce that the production will be moving on to London to share the experience with a wider audience."

Venue and dates for the London production have not been announced. Casting has also not been confirmed, but let's hope as many of the original cast members as possible will reprise their roles. The Mad King is directed by Dominic Cooke and written by Duncan Macmillan ( Every Brilliant Thing ).

highlights.title: OpenAI is building a humanoid robot, but the body isn't the real challenge
highlights.summary: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman wants a humanoid that can operate in a world designed for people, though the CEO says a robot 'brain' is a much bigger challenge.
body: Figuring out how the 'brain' will work will take a lot of time.
While OpenAI is already busy with the development of AI models and new consumer hardware, CEO Sam Altman and his team apparently have time for one more project: a humanoid robot.

On the Sources podcast, Altman explained that the human form is logical because "the world is very much designed for people." Doors, keyboards and tools are all designed around a certain type of body, and a robot that can move around in the same spaces should probably have a similar form factor. As Altman put it, "matching that form factor seems good."

When asked if OpenAI will actually build one, his response was much more succinct: "We will." However, Altman isn't so concerned with the nitty-gritty details of what that robot looks like. Those questions are "less important than really figuring out... the brain that makes the robot work," he said. Basically, giving a machine two arms and two legs doesn't get you very far if it doesn't know what to do with them.

What was originally intended to be a public release for the Drunken Goddess Reflux demo has now been canceled in favor of a "closed play session for a limited number of participants." It's a last-minute move Alliance Arts apologized for, but its concerns related to rapidly advancing AI technology were simply too great to ignore.

"We are concerned that, based on the content of the demo, works imitating or replicating this game's presentation and gameplay could be quickly produced using AI or other tools and released ahead of the game's launch," the developers said in their list of concerns.

In other words, sending a demo out into the wild could open the door for nefarious individuals to use AI to generate a low-effort clone or copycat experience. For a team hoping for a successful launch in just a few months, someone coming in to steal its thunder could potentially throw a wrench into things.
points: The developer behind Russian roulette anime game Drunken Goddess Reflux has canceled its plans for a public Steam demo, citing concerns over potential AI copycats.

highlights.title: How Australia’s tipping culture got awkward – and what to do about it
highlights.summary: Ten per cent, 20%, 25%? If you’ve made a cashless payment at a cafe or pub lately there’s a reasonable chance you’ve been prompted to tip. Isabella Lee looks into the arrival of US-style tip requests and where that money really goes.
body: Alyx: You’ve been thinking about tipping for a few months now, and wrote about it this week. What first sparked your interest? Isabella: I came across a post in a bartenders’ Facebook group from someone asking if their experience of having tips withheld was normal. The comments shocked me! There were more than 30 responses, with the majority of them calling out venues where they’d also been denied their tips. It made me think, if this practice was so common, why hadn’t anything been done about it?

Alyx: When you did some more digging, what did you find out? Isabella: I reached out to Fair Work to ask what legislation there was around paying out tips to staff. They told me there is none. So the original poster hadn’t experienced wage theft because the employers weren’t actually breaking any rules. It’s not just management who can dip their hand in the tip jar. Cashless payment systems take a percentage from every transaction made too. It’s pretty cheeky that the systems that allow a business to ask for tips – which changes customers’ decision-making behaviour – also get a cut.

highlights.title: Mercedes-AMG’s first ground-up SUV is a 1,150hp electric beast
highlights.summary: Earlier this year, Mercedes' AMG performance brand grabbed our attention with the GT four-door coupe, a souped-up sports sedan with three axial flux motors delivering over 1,150 horsepower.
body: It may even out-muscle the Porsche Cayenne Turbo Electric and Lucid Gravity.

The AMG GT SUV (say that five times fast) marks the first time in the performance brand’s 59-year history that it has developed a full-size SUV entirely in-house from the ground up. Scheduled to hit the US next summer, the new EV is built on Merc’s high-performance AMG.EA architecture to combine sports-car handling with full-size SUV suburban practicality.

It will be available in three trims — GT 53, GT 55, and the flagship GT 63 — with the top model delivering 1,153hp via the same three axial flux motors powering the four-door coupe. That beats the Porsche Cayenne Turbo Electric with Launch Control, which is sure to make for some awkward run-ins around Stuttgart.

Thanks to an 800-volt architecture, the SUV supports blistering-fast charging speeds up to 710kW on the 128kWh battery (GT 63 / GT 55) and 600kW on the 106kWh battery (GT 53). Drivers can charge 10–80 percent in 12 minutes or gain up to 450km (around 280 miles) of WLTP range in just 10 minutes. The 128kWh battery trims will have an estimated max range of 435 miles.

Kagiso Rabada insists there is no lingering bad blood with Australia as the South Africa speedster prepares to return to the site of his controversial clash with Steve…
body: Rabada has been declared fit to come back from his hamstring tear and face Australia in the second Test at St George’s Park, in his first match since May. The South African’s return comes at a crucial point in the series, with the hosts fighting to stay alive after their 214-run pumping in Durban last week.
But it is also timely, given it was at St George’s Park where Rabada was initially banned for two Tests for colliding with Smith while celebrating taking his wicket in 2018.

Rabada ultimately had his ban downgraded to a fine, leaving Smith and Australia unhappy that the batter was not able to speak at the hearing. The shoulder bump, and ensuing appeal, was one of the final flash points of the ill-spirited series before the ball-tampering scandal overshadowed it all.

Rabada has played against Australia 23 times across all formats since then without issue, while also being a teammate to some in franchise leagues. Speaking to local media before Sunday’s return, the 31-year-old made it clear he had no ill will towards Smith, even if he couldn’t see the pair meeting for coffee.

highlights.title: Websites are closing their doors to AI agents
highlights.summary: Autonomous agents are the hottest thing in AI. OpenAI, Meta, Google, Instinct, and others promise their agents can scour the internet on your behalf, doing anything from booking a dinner reservation and cleaning out your inbox to buying new shoes.
body: OpenAI, Meta, and Google want AI agents to do everything for you. But popular services on the web aren’t letting that happen.

In recent weeks, users of services like Meta’s Muse, xAI’s Grok, OpenAI’s Dots, and Instinct have reported blocks preventing their AI agents from performing tasks across top websites. Yelp told TechCrunch that it only allows AI agents that pay for its data licensing program, while Delta Air Lines is preventing them from booking tickets on behalf of users. JPMorgan Chase and Charles Schwab have also confirmed that they’re blocking AI agents from accessing accounts due to security concerns. Some users say sites that previously worked with their AI agent are no longer accessible, including Cars.com and Amtrak, suggesting other companies could be quietly blocking them.

highlights.title: The moment I knew: For Valentine’s Day he gave me a heart covered in fake blood. I was appalled – and thrilled
highlights.summary: Will Huxley thought Garrett looked like a Heathcliff type. They bonded over their shared love of Kate Bush. Then one day Garrett handed over an ornate gift box. Find more stories from the moment I knew series.
body: I n 2006 I’d just graduated film school at the Victorian College of the Arts and was working at the ABC in Melbourne. It was a pretty tumultuous time of my life. I had just broken up with my best friend and high school sweetheart – whom I adored – and was in the process of coming out.

I was drinking too much and in breaks from the chaos I’d find myself drawn to the local video store. That’s where I first saw Garrett behind the counter. I had an instant crush on him and spent a lot of time perusing the art house section, so he would see how creative and cultured I was.
I never had the guts to talk to him but one night in spring we ran into each other at a party. We hit it off and arranged a date at a cafe in the city.

I was obsessed with Kate Bush and Wuthering Heights, and Garrett struck me as this sort of Heathcliff type; he was a dark, handsome artist with very dramatic, gothic vibes. That day we talked about art and the things that we love. I was so excited that he shared my passion for Kate Bush, and listening to Hounds of Love on repeat. We talked about John Waters and Cindy Sherman and all these artists that were really formative for us.

highlights.title: Why it's important to monitor your PC's background processes
highlights.summary: What your PC is doing in the background doesn't need to be a mystery. Learn about what's happening and how to spot when something looks wrong.
body: Knowing what normally runs on your PC helps you spot when something isn't right.

Your PC is always doing something, even when you've closed all the app windows from your desktop. Windows is checking for updates and keeping everything moving under the hood, with other apps still running quietly in the background. Ideally, this is all happening with a useful purpose. But some apps or services are always going to use more processing power or memory than you expect, taking up resources that could otherwise be available to apps you actually want to use.

With that in mind, it's smart to get into the habit of checking your PC's background processes. When you know what's supposed to run, it'll help you spot the unusual. This doesn't mean you need to watch the numbers all day, and a long running list isn't bad by itself. Instead, monitoring them means you can spot processes causing problems or sucking up resources on your PC. That'll help you decide what to leave alone and what to close, especially when your PC starts to feel slow.

highlights.title: Why AI Isn’t Ready to Tackle Our Convoluted Genomes
highlights.summary: The DNA inside our cells isn’t just a series of instructions, but something far more dynamic. Like scientists, AI models don't yet have the data to properly decode it.
body: Since its molecular structure was deduced in the 1950s, DNA has been hailed by many biologists as the secret of life. They’ve read and studied the information stored in the DNA found in the cells of living organisms, known as their genomes, and claimed that this genetic database must be some kind of blueprint, code script, or computer. But if DNA really does harbor some greater secret about how life works, biologists have yet to find it.

In fact, the human genome is less a script than a puzzle that gets harder the closer they look. Knowing the entire sequence —the order of all 3 billion or so of our DNA’s chemical building blocks, nearly fully deduced by the international Human Genome Project between 1990 and 2003—hasn’t helped much. That investigation showed that barely 2 percent of the human genome consists of actual genes, the information-coding sequences of DNA.
points: The DNA inside our cells isn’t just a series of instructions, but something far more dynamic.
Like scientists, AI models don't yet have the data to properly decode it.

Battlefield Studios took to its official Discord server to offer background information on two skins that caused a stir with the launch of Battlefield 6 Season 5 this past week (via MP1st…
body: The cosmetics – one with what appeared to be a typo in the word "security" and another featuring infantry sporting a whopping five pistol holsters – were officially added October 13 and almost immediately drew ire from fans. It's that pesky misspelling, which took the shape of the non-existent word "security" on the armband of a McNeil skin, that the developers say will be fixed when Battlefield 6 Season 5 launches in November.
"You called it out clearly, and we hear your concerns," the message, acknowledging the memes and conversations surrounding the new skins, said.

The note continued: "To be completely frank: Items that miss the mark like this do not reflect the quality standards you expect from us, or that we set for ourselves. We take pride in the craft of our world and our gear, and seeing visual oddities slip through is frustrating for everyone. We are currently examining our internal processes and workflows to pinpoint how these issues occurred and to see how we can tighten our quality control process going forward. Thank you for holding us to high standards."

highlights.title: James McAvoy Says ‘Split’ Is The Only Film That ‘Really Consistently Pays Me’
highlights.summary: James McAvoy has starred in films including “Speak No Evil,” “Atonement” and “X-Men: First Class,” but he recently revealed the “only” film he still consistently receives residuals from is M.
body: In “Split,” three girls are kidnapped by a man with a diagnosed 23 distinct personalities (McAvoy). “They must try to escape before the apparent emergence of a frightful new 24th,” per the film’s official description. Anya Taylor-Joy, Haley Lu Richardson and Jessica Sula starred alongside McAvoy. The film, which cost just $6 million to make, went on to gross $138.29 million domestically and $140.16 million internationally for a $278.45 million worldwide total.
McAvoy also spoke about Shyamalan and his experience working with the director.

“I very consciously took from many of the directors that I worked with, and subconsciously as well, but the thing I took away from him is his preparedness,” McAvoy said. “He made that film, and [sequel] ‘Glass,’ on incredibly modest budgets, and very focused on how he would maximize his day and maximize his shots and maximize what he got out of the story by just being incredibly well-prepared and being able to share that and communicate that with the crew.”
